content: Epidural Abscess Spinal Epidural Abscess For the treatment of a spinal epidural abscess, empiric antimicrobial therapy is initiated to cover a broad range of potential pathogens. The preferred regimen includes a loading dose of vancomycin at 25–30 mg/kg administered intravenously, followed by a maintenance dose of 15–20 mg/kg intravenously every 8–12 hours for a duration of 2–4 weeks. This is then transitioned to oral therapy to complete a total treatment duration of 6–8 weeks. Additionally, ceftriaxone at a dose of 2 grams intravenously every 24 hours is administered for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Culture-Directed Antimicrobial Therapy Penicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus: The preferred treatment is penicillin G at 4 million units intravenously every 4 hours for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Methicillin-Susceptible Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus: Options include cefazolin 2 grams intravenously every 8 hours, nafcillin 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours, or oxacillin 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours, each for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Alternatively, clindamycin 600 mg intravenously every 6 hours can be used for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA): The preferred regimen is vancomycin with a loading dose of 25–30 mg/kg intravenously, followed by 15–20 mg/kg intravenously every 8–12 hours for 2–4 weeks, then transitioned to oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Streptococcus: Penicillin G at 3–4 million units intravenously every 4 hours or ampicillin 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours is recommended for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Enterococcus: The preferred treatment is penicillin G at 3–4 million units intravenously every 4 hours or ampicillin 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Enterobacteriaceae: Ceftriaxone 1–2 grams intravenously every 12 hours or cefotaxime 2 grams intravenously every 6–8 hours is recommended for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Gram-Negative Bacteria: Ceftazidime 2 grams intravenously every 8 hours or cefepime 2 grams intravenously every 12 hours is preferred for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Alternatively, ciprofloxacin 400 mg intravenously every 12 hours, levofloxacin 750 mg intravenously every 24 hours, or moxifloxacin 400 mg intravenously every 24 hours can be used for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Anaerobes: Metronidazole 500 mg intravenously every 6 hours is the preferred treatment for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Mixed Infections (Staphylococcus, Gram-Negative Bacteria, and Anaerobes): Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 grams intravenously every 6 hours, ticarcillin-clavulanate 3.1 grams intravenously every 4 hours, or piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 grams intravenously every 4–6 hours is recommended for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Alternatively, imipenem 500–1000 mg intravenously every 6 hours or meropenem 1–2 grams intravenously every 8 hours can be used for 2–4 weeks, followed by oral therapy to complete 6–8 weeks. Brain Abscess Bacterial Brain Abscess For bacterial brain abscesses of unknown origin, empiric antimicrobial therapy is initiated. The preferred regimen includes vancomycin at 15–20 mg/kg intravenously every 8–12 hours for 6–8 weeks, followed by oral therapy for an additional 2–3 months. This is combined with either cefotaxime 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours or ceftriaxone 2 grams intravenously every 12 hours for 6–8 weeks, followed by oral therapy for 2–3 months. Additionally, metronidazole is administered at 7.5 mg/kg intravenously every 6 hours or 15 mg/kg intravenously every 12 hours for 6–8 weeks, followed by oral therapy for 2–3 months. An alternative regimen includes penicillin G at 3–4 million units intravenously every 4 hours for 6–8 weeks, combined with either cefotaxime 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours or ceftriaxone 2 grams intravenously every 12 hours for 6–8 weeks, followed by oral therapy for 2–3 months. Metronidazole is also included in this regimen at the same dosing schedule. Specific Considerations Nocardia: The preferred treatment involves trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) at a dose of 15 mg/kg/day of the TMP component and 75 mg/kg/day of the SMX component, administered intravenously or orally every 6–12 hours, combined with imipenem 500 mg intravenously every 6 hours. If there is involvement of multiple organs, amikacin at 7.5 mg/kg intravenously every 12 hours may be added. An alternative regimen includes linezolid 600 mg intravenously or orally every 12 hours combined with meropenem 2 grams intravenously every 8 hours. Tuberculous Brain Abscess: Treatment regimens for tuberculous brain abscesses are not detailed in this section. Fungal Brain Abscess: Treatment regimens for fungal brain abscesses are not detailed in this section.
